[PROPOSEDI ORDER
This matter is before the Court on Plaintiff's Motion for Priority Determination and
Sequencing of Pending Proceedings Concerning ECF No. 96 (ECF No. _ (the "Motion"). Upon
consideration of the Motion, the Memorandum in Support, any response and reply, and the record,
and for good cause shown, it is hereby
ORDERED as follows:
The Motion is GRANTED. The Court has given the Motion priority consideration
and determines it on the papers under Local Civil Rule 7(J) and Federal Rule of Civil Procedure
78(b).
To the extent authorized under the operative referral, Magistrate Judge William E.
Fitzpatrick shall give priority consideration to Plaintiff's Rule 54(b) Motion to Vacate ECF No.
1

96 and Determine Magistrate Judge Davis's Ownership of Meta Common Stock (ECF No. _
(the "Rule 54(b) Motion"').
3.
Final determination by the District Judge of the following matters (the
"Overlapping ECF No. 96 Issues") is DEFERRED until disposition of the Rule 54(b) Motion or
further order of the District Judge:
(a) whether ECF No. 96 should be set aside, modified, or given limited effect, as
requested in ECF Nos. 97-99; and
(b)
the historical ownership and holding-arrangement facts identified in ECF No. 931
5, with any relief under ECF No. 93 that depends on them.
Upon disposition of the Rule 54(b) Motion, the District Judge will complete
review of the Overlapping ECF No. 96 Issues with that disposition available. That disposition
remains subject to timely objection under Federal Rule of Civil Procedure 72(a).
The District Judge retains authority over the referral. Nothing in this Order limits
the District Judge's determination at any time of any independent or threshold issue. Those issues
include the referral and successor-designation questions presented in ECF No. 93 9 10(R1) and
ECF No. 97 11 15 and 20(6), and independently warranted relief under ECF No. 93. If the District
Judge determines that the Rule 54(b) Motion falls outside the operative referral, the deferral in
paragraph 3 ends upon that determination.
6.
This Order does not stay this action. It does not defer or decide ECF Nos. 10, 21,
or 45. No pending objection or motion is withdrawn. No deadline is extended or restarted. The
briefing on ECF No. 93 is not reopened.
2
